stimulus.content: "I was going to grab lunch before the seminar, but there's no time now."

options.A: I usually have lunch at the café downstairs.
options.B: Yeah, let's just head straight there.
options.C: The seminar was really interesting.
options.D: I ate there last week too.

explanation: O falante sinaliza falta de tempo; a resposta natural propõe a ação consequente. (A) reaproveita lunch sem reagir à falta de tempo; (C)/(D) ignoram a urgência.

stimulus.content: "Do you mind if I borrow your notes from Tuesday? I was out sick."

options.A: Sure, I'll send them over tonight.
options.B: I hope you feel better soon.
options.C: I borrowed a book from the library on Tuesday.
options.D: Tuesday's class starts at nine.

explanation: A um pedido direto, a resposta natural é aceitar e combinar um plano. (B) é gentil, mas não responde ao pedido; (C) e (D) só repetem palavras da fala (borrow, Tuesday).

stimulus.content: "Honestly, I'm not sure this draft is ready to submit."

options.A: I'm sure the printer is ready.
options.B: What do you think it still needs?
options.C: I submitted mine yesterday.
options.D: That's a great title.

explanation: Diante da insegurança sobre o rascunho, a resposta natural procura o problema específico. (A) repete ready sem tratar da preocupação; (C) e (D) ignoram a preocupação.

stimulus.content: "You're not still planning to walk in this weather, are you?"

options.A: No, I'll catch the bus instead.
options.B: The weather report comes on at six.
options.C: I walked there yesterday.
options.D: It rained a lot last semester too.

explanation: A pergunta retórica é um alerta educado sobre ir a pé com esse tempo, e a resposta natural muda o plano. (B) só repete weather; (C) e (D) falam de outro momento e ignoram o alerta.

stimulus.content: "I heard the registrar's office changed their hours."

options.A: I registered for four classes this term.
options.B: Really? Do you know the new schedule?
options.C: The office is on the second floor.
options.D: I haven't registered for anything yet.

explanation: Diante de uma informação nova (a mudança de horário), a resposta natural mostra interesse e pede um detalhe. (A) e (D) aproveitam o som de registrar em register (matricular-se), mas não reagem à notícia; (C) dá a localização do escritório, que ninguém perguntou.

stimulus.content: "Could you run your presentation by me before the meeting?"

options.A: I ran three miles this morning.
options.B: Sure, are you free around four?
options.C: The meeting's been moved to Thursday.
options.D: I gave my first presentation in high school.

explanation: "Run X by me" é "me mostrar antes", e a resposta natural marca um horário. (A) toma "run" ao pé da letra; (C) muda o foco; (D) repete presentation sem responder ao pedido.

stimulus.content: "I thought the lab report was due next week, not tomorrow."

options.A: So did I. Let me double-check the syllabus.
options.B: The lab is on the ground floor.
options.C: I finished my report last month.
options.D: Next week works better for me too.

explanation: Diante da dúvida sobre a data, a resposta natural é conferir junto no syllabus. (B), (C) e (D) ignoram a dúvida.

stimulus.content: "Would you rather present first or last?"

options.A: The last presentation ran over time.
options.B: Last, if that's an option. I need time to prepare.
options.C: The presentation is worth 20% of the grade.
options.D: First place goes to the best presentation.

explanation: Numa pergunta de preferência (primeiro ou último), a resposta natural escolhe e justifica. (A), (C) e (D) não respondem à escolha oferecida.

stimulus.content: "This bus is taking forever. We should've left earlier."

options.A: The bus stop is right over there.
options.B: Tell me about it. I hate cutting it this close.
options.C: I take this bus every day.
options.D: I left my umbrella on the bus once.

explanation: Diante da reclamação sobre a demora, "Tell me about it" concorda com ênfase e acrescenta algo. (A), (C) e (D) repetem bus ou left sem reagir à reclamação.

stimulus.content: "Professor Lin said she might cancel Friday's class."

options.A: She's a great lecturer, isn't she?
options.B: Did she say why, or was it just a maybe?
options.C: Friday's class is in the east building.
options.D: I've never had a class canceled before.

explanation: Diante de uma notícia incerta ("might cancel"), a resposta natural pede esclarecimento sobre o motivo ou a certeza. (A), (C) e (D) desviam do assunto.

stimulus.content: "I've been meaning to ask: how did the interview go?"

options.A: It's at two o'clock on Thursday.
options.B: Better than I expected, actually. They said they'd call by Friday.
options.C: I've had a lot of interviews lately.
options.D: The company is downtown, near the station.

explanation: A pergunta é sobre como foi a entrevista, e a resposta natural conta o resultado e o próximo passo. (A) responde sobre horário; (C) e (D) generalizam ou desviam.

stimulus.content: "Do you think it's worth applying? I doubt I'd get in."

options.A: The application fee is fifty dollars.
options.B: You never know unless you try. I'd go for it.
options.C: I applied there two years ago.
options.D: The program starts in September.

explanation: Diante de dúvida e autocrítica, a resposta natural é encorajar. (A), (C) e (D) desviam para custo, experiência passada e calendário.

stimulus.content: "Excuse me, is this seat next to you taken?"

options.A: No, go right ahead and sit down.
options.B: Yes, I took the exam yesterday.
options.C: The seats in the back are blue.
options.D: I usually sit near the window.

explanation: Quando alguém pergunta is this seat next to you taken?, quer saber se o lugar está livre para sentar, por isso (A) responde com naturalidade ao liberar o assento. Se você pensou em (B), repare que ela usa o verbo took, mas fala de uma prova de ontem e não do lugar ao lado.

stimulus.content: "Oh, wait, I left my student ID card in my dorm room."

options.A: My dorm room is on the third floor.
options.B: We can wait here while you grab it.
options.C: The student center closes at eight.
options.D: I got my new card last September.

explanation: Ao dizer I left my student ID card in my dorm room, quem fala percebe que esqueceu o cartão agora, e (B) traz a reação prática de esperar enquanto a pessoa busca o documento. A opção (A) é uma armadilha comum porque repete dorm room, mas só informa o andar do quarto sem ajudar na situação.

stimulus.content: "Do you know what time the campus bookstore closes today?"

options.A: I bought two notebooks there yesterday.
options.B: The bookstore is right across the quad.
options.C: I think it closes at five today.
options.D: Yes, the textbooks are pretty expensive.

explanation: A pergunta what time the campus bookstore closes today pede o horário de fechamento da livraria, que (C) informa de modo natural. Já a alternativa (B) fala da localização da loja no campus, respondendo a onde ela fica e não a que horas fecha.

stimulus.content: "It's a bit cold in this classroom, don't you think?"

options.A: Class starts at ten every Monday.
options.B: Winter is my favorite season here.
options.C: I think the professor is outside.
options.D: Yeah, I'll go shut the window now.

explanation: O comentário It's a bit cold in this classroom, don't you think? busca concordância sobre o frio na sala, e (D) concorda e oferece uma solução fechando a janela. A opção (B) puxa o assunto para o inverno em geral e ignora o desconforto da sala agora.

stimulus.content: "I can't find the biology lab on this campus map."

options.A: I'm heading there now, so follow me.
options.B: Biology is a required class for me.
options.C: The campus map is free for students.
options.D: Our lab partner finished the chart.

explanation: Diante da dificuldade em I can't find the biology lab on this campus map, quem fala precisa de ajuda para chegar ao local, e (A) resolve isso ao convidar para ir junto. A alternativa (C) repete campus map, mas fala do preço do mapa em vez de indicar o caminho.

stimulus.content: "Are you still using that dictionary, or can I borrow it?"

options.A: I looked up three new words today.
options.B: It's all yours, I'm done with it.
options.C: The library has a lot of computers.
options.D: You can buy one at the main store.

explanation: A pergunta Are you still using that dictionary, or can I borrow it? é um pedido para usar o dicionário agora, e (B) responde de forma direta ao avisar que já terminou de usar. A opção (A) fala de palavras pesquisadas no dia, mas não diz se o livro está livre.

stimulus.content: "I'm swamped with readings this week, so I might skip the club meeting."

options.A: The reading room on the second floor is quiet.
options.B: Our club meets every Wednesday in the lounge.
options.C: No worries, I'll fill you in on what you miss.
options.D: I finished reading that chapter last weekend.

explanation: Quando quem fala avisa I'm swamped with readings this week, so I might skip the club meeting, está explicando que deve faltar à reunião por excesso de leitura, e (C) acolhe a ausência e promete passar o resumo depois. A opção (B) apenas informa o dia fixo do encontro, sem reagir ao aviso de falta.

stimulus.content: "Did you manage to get a seat in Professor Patel's seminar for next term?"

options.A: Her office hours are on Tuesday afternoons.
options.B: The seminar room is in the history building.
options.C: I took an introductory class with her once.
options.D: No, it filled up fast, so I'm on the waitlist.

explanation: A pergunta Did you manage to get a seat in Professor Patel's seminar trata de conseguir vaga na matrícula, e (D) responde diretamente ao contar que a turma lotou e restou a lista de espera da disciplina. A alternativa (B) confunde get a seat na matéria com a localização física da sala.

stimulus.content: "Wait, didn't the teaching assistant say the quiz would only cover chapter four?"

options.A: Actually, she added chapter five in an email.
options.B: The teaching assistant grades all our papers.
options.C: Chapter four was much shorter than the others.
options.D: We have a short quiz every other Friday morning.

explanation: Ao perguntar didn't the teaching assistant say the quiz would only cover chapter four?, quem fala quer confirmar a matéria do teste, e (A) esclarece a dúvida com a atualização enviada por e-mail. A opção (C) comenta o tamanho do capítulo quatro, mas não confirma o conteúdo cobrado na avaliação.

stimulus.content: "If we don't reserve a group study room soon, they'll all be booked for finals."

options.A: The library bought new tables last month.
options.B: Good point, I'll log in and book one now.
options.C: Final exams always last for a whole week.
options.D: Our study group has four people this term.

explanation: O alerta If we don't reserve a group study room soon, they'll all be booked aponta a urgência de garantir uma sala antes que acabe, e (B) reage na hora ao fazer a reserva no sistema. A alternativa (D) fala do tamanho do grupo de estudo, mas deixa de lado o risco de ficar sem sala.

stimulus.content: "I was hoping to talk to my advisor today, but her door's closed."

options.A: My advisor helped me pick my major last year.
options.B: The door to the main building locks at nine.
options.C: She's usually back from lunch around one-thirty.
options.D: Advising appointments take about twenty minutes.

explanation: Diante da frustração em I was hoping to talk to my advisor today, but her door's closed, a resposta mais prestativa é informar quando ela deve voltar, como faz (C) ao indicar o horário de retorno do almoço. A opção (B) repete a palavra door, mas fala da porta do prédio à noite.

stimulus.content: "How come you're printing your slides here instead of at the computer lab?"

options.A: I need about fifteen slides for my talk.
options.B: The computer lab is in the north wing.
options.C: Printing costs five cents a page there.
options.D: Both printers over there are jammed again.

explanation: Em How come you're printing your slides here instead of at the computer lab?, a expressão how come pede o motivo da escolha, e (D) apresenta a causa prática do problema nas impressoras do laboratório. A alternativa (B) apenas diz onde fica o laboratório, sem explicar a troca de lugar.

stimulus.content: "I'd double-check those survey numbers before sending the file to Dr. Evans, if I were you."

options.A: Dr. Evans teaches the advanced research methods course.
options.B: Did you spot an error in one of the spreadsheet columns?
options.C: How many students ended up responding to the survey?
options.D: The file was saved in the shared folder yesterday.

explanation: A estrutura I'd double-check those survey numbers... if I were you funciona como um alerta indireto de que algo parece errado nos dados, por isso (B) reage na hora perguntando se houve um erro específico na planilha. A opção (C) também faz uma pergunta sobre a pesquisa, mas ignora completamente o aviso de revisão.

stimulus.content: "Wait, so our funding proposal for the robotics project is still up in the air?"

options.A: The robotics team won second place at last year's fair.
options.B: Our project focuses on small aerial drones for mapping.
options.C: Yeah, the committee postponed its final vote until Monday.
options.D: The funding form needs to be signed in blue or black ink.

explanation: Na pergunta so our funding proposal for the robotics project is still up in the air?, a expressão up in the air significa indefinido, o que (C) confirma ao explicar o adiamento da votação final. A alternativa (B) é uma armadilha clássica porque leva in the air ao pé da letra e fala de drones aéreos.

stimulus.content: "I was under the impression that the internship required a letter from the dean."

options.A: The dean's office moved to the administration building.
options.B: Internships are a great way to build work experience.
options.C: I wrote a cover letter for that position last night.
options.D: Actually, they dropped that requirement this year.

explanation: A abertura I was under the impression that... indica uma suposição que pede confirmação ou correção, e (D) corrige a suposição ao contar que a exigência caiu este ano. A opção (C) repete a palavra letter, mas troca a carta da direção por uma carta de apresentação pessoal.

stimulus.content: "We'd better iron out the timeline for our lab experiment before we meet with the TA."

options.A: Agreed, let's sit down after lunch and map out each step.
options.B: The lab equipment is made of stainless steel and iron.
options.C: Our teaching assistant holds office hours on Wednesdays.
options.D: The experiment took much longer than anyone expected.

explanation: Em We'd better iron out the timeline for our lab experiment, o phrasal verb iron out quer dizer acertar os detalhes pendentes, e (A) concorda propondo definir cada etapa depois do almoço. A alternativa (B) cai na armadilha literal de iron como ferro ou metal do equipamento.

stimulus.content: "You didn't happen to pick up an extra copy of the syllabus on your way out, did you?"

options.A: The syllabus lists three major papers for this semester.
options.B: I dropped that class during the first week of the term.
options.C: No, sorry, but the professor posted the PDF online too.
options.D: The copy machine in the department lounge is working.

explanation: A pergunta You didn't happen to pick up an extra copy of the syllabus... did you? é um jeito educado de pedir uma cópia caso a pessoa tenha pego uma a mais, e (C) responde e indica a versão em PDF online. A opção (D) aproveita a palavra copy para falar da copiadora, sem responder ao pedido.

stimulus.content: "Getting a summer research grant as a first-year student is a bit of a long shot, isn't it?"

options.A: Maybe, but a couple of freshmen got funded last summer.
options.B: The photography club is taking shots of the campus quad.
options.C: Summer classes run from early June through mid-August.
options.D: Grant applications must be submitted to the main office.

explanation: Quando quem fala diz que conseguir a bolsa no primeiro ano é a bit of a long shot, quer dizer que a chance parece baixa, e (A) reconhece a dificuldade mas anima com exemplos reais do verão passado. A alternativa (B) interpreta shot ao pé da letra como foto, fugindo do assunto.

stimulus.content: "Well, the peer reviewers didn't exactly jump for joy over our methodology section."

options.A: The methodology section comes right after the introduction.
options.B: I'm glad the reviewers were so enthusiastic about our work.
options.C: Peer review for that journal usually takes about six weeks.
options.D: That's rough, but hopefully their comments are easy to fix.

explanation: Ao dizer que os pareceristas didn't exactly jump for joy over our methodology section, quem fala usa uma atenuação irônica para contar que a seção recebeu críticas, e (D) capta esse tom ao lamentar o revés e focar nos ajustes. A opção (B) perde a ironia do didn't exactly e acha que o retorno foi entusiasmado.

stimulus.content: "Since our archive access was denied, I guess we're back to square one on the thesis topic."

options.A: Not necessarily, we could use the digitized collection instead.
options.B: The main archive is located in the basement of the old library.
options.C: Square tables work best when we have a large seminar discussion.
options.D: Our thesis advisor approved the initial outline two months ago.

explanation: Em I guess we're back to square one on the thesis topic, a expressão back to square one indica a sensação de ter de recomeçar do zero, e (A) responde propondo uma alternativa viável com o acervo digitalizado. A opção (D) cita a aprovação antiga do esboço e ignora o bloqueio atual ao arquivo.

stimulus.content: "Had I known Professor Kim's seminar was this heavy on econometrics, I'd have audited it instead."

options.A: Professor Kim earned her doctorate in economics ten years ago.
options.B: The add-drop window's still open if you want to switch status.
options.C: Auditing a course means you don't receive a letter grade for it.
options.D: The seminar meets twice a week in the graduate wing downstairs.

explanation: A inversão condicional Had I known... I'd have audited it instead expressa arrependimento por não cursar a disciplina apenas como ouvinte, e (B) traz uma saída prática lembrando que o prazo de ajuste ainda permite mudar a modalidade. A alternativa (C) explica o que é audit, algo que quem fala já domina.

stimulus.content: "Look, far be it from me to tell you how to structure your talk, but ten case studies in fifteen minutes?"

options.A: The conference panel allots fifteen minutes to each presenter.
options.B: Case studies are widely used in qualitative social research.
options.C: Fair point, I should probably trim it down to two or three.
options.D: Your presentation last semester was really well structured.

explanation: Mesmo suavizada por far be it from me, a pergunta final but ten case studies in fifteen minutes? é uma crítica educada ao excesso de exemplos para pouco tempo, e (C) entende o recado ao reduzir a quantidade de casos. A opção (A) apenas repete a regra dos quinze minutos sem resolver a sobrecarga.

stimulus.content: "Take what the department chair said about next year's teaching fellowships with a grain of salt."

options.A: The department chair's term ends after the spring semester.
options.B: Teaching fellowships cover full tuition plus a small stipend.
options.C: The campus dining hall cut back on salt in most of its meals.
options.D: Right, nothing's official until the budget is signed in May.

explanation: A expressão take... with a grain of salt recomenda cautela diante do que foi dito sobre as bolsas de monitoria, e (D) acompanha esse cuidado lembrando que nada é oficial antes da assinatura do orçamento. A alternativa (B) descreve os benefícios da bolsa, mas ignora o alerta de incerteza.

stimulus.content: "I wouldn't put off booking the spectrometer if you want your samples analyzed before the colloquium."

options.A: The annual colloquium features speakers from three universities.
options.B: True, the lab sign-up sheet always fills up weeks in advance.
options.C: I put the spectrometer manual back on the top shelf yesterday.
options.D: The rock samples were collected during our field trip in June.

explanation: Em I wouldn't put off booking the spectrometer, o phrasal verb put off significa adiar, então a fala aconselha a reservar o aparelho logo, e (B) concorda lembrando que a agenda do equipamento lota semanas antes. A opção (C) confunde put off com guardar um manual na estante.

stimulus.title: Listen and Choose a Response
stimulus.content: **ÁUDIO 1 (transcrição):** **Man:** "Would you mind if I borrowed your notes from Tuesday's lecture? I was out sick."

prompt: Which response best continues the exchange?

options.A: "Sure, I'll email them to you tonight."
options.B: "I hope you feel better soon."
options.C: "The lecture was about economic policy."
options.D: "I wasn't in class either."

explanation: resposta direta ao pedido

stimulus.title: Listen and Choose a Response
stimulus.content: **ÁUDIO 2:** **Woman:** "Have you decided whether you're presenting first or second on Friday?"

options.A: "The presentation is in room 120."
options.B: "I'd rather go first, if that's okay with you."
options.C: "Friday is my busiest day."
options.D: "I haven't finished reading the article."

stimulus.title: Listen and Choose a Response
stimulus.content: **ÁUDIO 3:** **Man:** "I emailed the professor two days ago and still haven't heard back."

options.A: "The professor's office is on the second floor."
options.B: "I sent mine last week."
options.C: "I think the email server was down on Monday, so try again."
options.D: "You should present first."

explanation: (nota: a opção (C) aponta uma causa provável e sugere uma ação prática, enquanto (A) e (B) apenas repetem o assunto de professor ou e-mail sem responder à queixa.)

stimulus.title: Listen and Choose a Response
stimulus.content: **ÁUDIO 4:** **Woman:** "This reading is forty pages — there's no way I'll finish it before class."

options.A: "The class is at ten."
options.B: "Focus on the intro and the conclusion. That's usually enough to follow the discussion."
options.C: "I bought the book last semester."
options.D: "There are forty students in that class."

stimulus.title: Listen and Choose a Response
stimulus.content: **Woman:** "I can't believe how much the printer fees went up this semester."

options.A: "Yeah, I switched to printing at the library instead."
options.B: "The printer is out of paper again."
options.C: "I registered for four classes this semester."
options.D: "The library closes at nine."
